def decide(bars, account):
    """Enter on a 0.5% break above a rising 100-day average; re-enter on a confirmed golden-cross uptrend; exit on an 8% trailing stop from the highest close since entry."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    n = 100
    if len(closes) < n + 20:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 100-day average and its slope"
    average = sum(closes[-n:]) / n
    prior_average = sum(closes[-n-20:-20]) / n
    price = closes[-1]
    entry_band = 0.005 * average
    rising = average > prior_average
    if account["position"] <= 0:
        if price > average + entry_band and rising:
            return "BUY", "close above a rising 100-day average"
        # confirmed-trend re-entry: price above rising 50-day and 50-day above 100-day
        m = 50
        if len(closes) >= m + 20:
            avg50 = sum(closes[-m:]) / m
            prior50 = sum(closes[-m-20:-20]) / m
            if price > avg50 and avg50 > prior50 and avg50 > average:
                return "BUY", "confirmed golden-cross uptrend re-entry"
    if account["position"] > 0:
        entry = account.get("entry_price")
        if entry is None:
            entry = price
        peak = price
        for c in reversed(closes):
            if c < entry:
                break
            if c > peak:
                peak = c
        if price < peak * 0.92:
            return "SELL", "8% trailing stop from the post-entry high"
    return "HOLD", "no change"

def decide(bars, account):
    """Hold while close is above a rising 100-day average; enter on a 0.5% break above, exit on a 2% break below."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    n = 100
    if len(closes) < n + 20:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 100-day average and its slope"
    average = sum(closes[-n:]) / n
    prior_average = sum(closes[-n-20:-20]) / n
    price = closes[-1]
    entry_band = 0.005 * average
    exit_band = 0.02 * average
    rising = average > prior_average
    if account["position"] <= 0 and price > average + entry_band and rising:
        return "BUY", "close above a rising 100-day average"
    if account["position"] > 0 and price < average - exit_band:
        return "SELL", "close is clearly below the 100-day average"
    return "HOLD", "no change"

Starting strategy supplied by the researcher and identical for every run; you did not write it. It is deliberately simple. Judge it on the evidence like any other version.
def decide(bars, account):
    """Seed strategy: hold the stock while its close is above the 20-day average."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    if len(closes) < 20:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 20-day average"
    average = sum(closes[-20:]) / 20
    price = closes[-1]
    if account["position"] <= 0 and price > average:
        return "BUY", "close is above the 20-day average"
    if account["position"] > 0 and price < average:
        return "SELL", "close is below the 20-day average"
    return "HOLD", "no change"

2024-W442024-11-04REVISE → rejectedv001-0.01%+0.99%-1.01The seed strategy is a pure 20-day MA crossover with no trend filter, no exit discipline beyond the same MA, and no protection against whipsaw. With only 1 live day there is no live evidence, but the design is weak: a 20-day MA on a single stock generates frequent round-trips (each costing 1bp) and gets chopped in sideways markets, and it has no way to distinguish a healthy uptrend from a dead-cat bounce. I am replacing it with a dual-confirmation trend system: enter only when price is above a rising 50-day MA AND the 20-day MA is above the 50-day MA (trend alignment), and exit when price closes below the 50-day MA or the 20-day MA crosses below the 50-day MA. This reduces trade count, keeps the position in sustained uptrends (which is what beats buy&hold on a single stock), and cuts losses faster than a bare 20-day MA. I also add a simple volatility-scaled stop from entry to cap drawdowns. This is a structural improvement, not a parameter tweak, and it should be tested over the full 276-bar history before adoption. 2024-W452024-11-11REVISE → rejectedv001+3.52%+2.93%-0.41The seed 20-day MA crossover has no trend filter and whipsaws: it buys late and sells on minor dips, and with only 6 live days it is already behind buy&hold (-0.44pp) while holding the stock most of the time anyway. The core flaw is that a fast single-MA exit cuts winners on noise. I replace it with a dual-MA trend regime (50-day above 200-day) plus a slower 50-day exit, so we stay long in uptrends and only exit on a genuine trend break, reducing churn and keeping exposure closer to buy&hold while still protecting against drawdowns.
